title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
statement: A sorted list of distinct integers has been rotated an unknown number of times. Return the smallest element in O(log n). The list is non-empty.

large_tests.gen_code:
def gen():
    a = list(range(200000))
    k = 77777
    return [a[k:] + a[:k]]

hints.1_question: Compare the middle element with something that tells you which side the minimum is on.
hints.2_nudge: If nums[mid] > nums[hi], the drop (and the minimum) is to the right of mid. Otherwise the minimum is at mid or to its left.
hints.3_big_hint: While lo < hi: mid; if nums[mid] > nums[hi]: lo = mid + 1 else hi = mid. Return nums[lo].

known_bugs.name: compares with nums[lo] instead of nums[hi]
known_bugs.followup: In an array that is not rotated at all, nums[mid] > nums[lo]. Does that mean the minimum is to the right?

known_bugs.name: lo = mid never makes progress
known_bugs.followup: With two elements, what is mid, and does lo = mid shrink the range?

known_bugs.name: returns the index instead of the value
known_bugs.followup: Re-read what the function is supposed to return: the minimum value or its position?

followups: What changes when duplicates are allowed (problem 154)?
Why compare against nums[hi] rather than nums[lo]?
